newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes off lows as buyers stay away.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes off lows as buyers stay away.

text.p: Cocoa futures drifted lower from the morning's firmer open as a weak New York compounded London's earlier losses amid a dearth of buyers, traders said on Monday.
Ivory Coast selling in the morning dragged values lower but the downside momentum was not enough to cause the benchmark March contract to test support just below 900 stg.
Traders said underlying support seemed reasonably solid even though buyers were staying away for the time being.
"Below the 900 level there will be some support, I think it's a good opportunity to buy," said one, citing lower Ghana purchases and potential problems with Ivory Coast shipping.
"I wouldn't be surprised if we see another bottom here, and I think the market is undervalued," he said.
Ghana cocoa purchases to the end of the seventh week of the 1996/97 season were a cumulative 149,906 tonnes compared with 208,658 tonnes at the end of the corresponding week of 1995/96.
Other traders said they expected market to be qui of its opening period this week, especially on Friday.
At the close March stood four stg down at 903 stg and May five lower at 922 stg. Volume was light at 2,320 lots.
